headline: A broad trade law that changes how U.S. customs agencies handle imports, exports, intellectual property, and travel, and raises the duty-free travel limit to $800.
what_it_does: The law sets rules and goals for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and related agencies on enforcing trade laws, speeding legal imports, and collecting duties. It targets evasion of antidumping and countervailing duties, requires CBP to help protect trademarks and copyrights at the border, and expands small business export help. It also raises the general duty-free limit for shipped goods from $200 to $800 and sets rules for airport preclearance operations abroad.

who_it_affects.how: They face new CBP priorities, risk-based bond amounts for new and nonresident importers, and new rules for customs brokers collecting importer information.

who_it_affects.group: Travelers and people receiving international shipments
who_it_affects.how: The duty-free limit for articles brought in by one person on one day rises from $200 to $800, and travelers get education on buying infringing goods abroad.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that export or trade
who_it_affects.how: The Small Business Administration must convene a working group during trade talks and state trade programs get grant authority through fiscal year 2020.
CBP may share product images and information with owners when imports are suspected of infringing their rights, unless an investigation or national security would be harmed.

who_it_affects.group: Domestic producers in antidumping and countervailing duty cases
who_it_affects.how: Interest on collected duties is added to CBP duty payments to affected domestic producers for qualifying expenses.

who_it_affects.group: Airports and passengers in certain foreign countries
who_it_affects.how: CBP may run preclearance operations there, and U.S. passenger carriers must have the same access as non-U.S. carriers.

who_it_affects.group: Individuals who file late federal tax returns
who_it_affects.how: The maximum civil penalty for failing to file within 60 days of the deadline rises from $135 to $205, adjusted yearly for inflation.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted February 24, 2016, but the summary gives no single general start date. Some parts have set dates, such as customs user fee authority through September 30, 2025, Nepal preferences ending after December 31, 2025, and ACE funding for fiscal years 2016 through 2018.
